items.title: Saliva test for endometriosis recommended for NHS use in draft NICE guidance
items.why: NICE early value guidance backs the Ziwig Endotest, a salivary micro-RNA test (109 miRNAs, sequencing plus AI; reported sensitivity around 97% and specificity around 94% in the 971-patient ENDOmiRNA study), and the EndoSure test as complementary diagnostic tools for an initial three years while real-world evidence is gathered. Aimed at cutting the roughly nine-year average diagnostic delay; laparoscopy remains the pathway standard, so read the guidance before quoting it in clinic.

items.title: Baroness Amos publishes the final report of the National Maternity and Neonatal Investigation
items.why: Eight recommendations for system-wide reform, including a statutory national Maternity and Neonatal Commissioner and national service standards, with findings that women are not being listened to and that racism and discrimination are embedded across maternity and neonatal care. A National Action Plan is due in December 2026; expect this to shape every UK unit's improvement agenda.

items.title: RCOG updates the placenta praevia & placenta accreta spectrum green-top guideline
items.why: The first update since 2018 strengthens early risk detection and recognises that PAS is not exclusively linked to placenta praevia or previous caesarean, reflecting evidence on other uterine surgical trauma (curettage, hysteroscopic surgery, ablation, UAE, myomectomy) and adding a new section on caesarean scar ectopic pregnancy. The Pocket O&G guide still reflects the 2018 edition until it is refreshed, so read the new guideline in full.

items.title: Six hours of intrauterine balloon tamponade non-inferior to 18 hours for PPH
items.why: In a US randomised trial of 64 women with atonic PPH after vaginal birth (Larrea et al, Obstet Gynecol 2026), removing the balloon at 6 hours was non-inferior to 18 hours for further blood loss, with no difference in escalation. Small and single-centre, so not yet guideline-changing, but it questions routine overnight balloon dwell times.

items.title: NICE clarifies the tachysystole definition in intrapartum care (NG235)
items.why: A May 2026 amendment defines uterine tachysystole within hyperstimulation as 5 or more contractions per 10 minutes for at least 20 minutes, aligning NG235 with the fetal monitoring guideline and BNF advice on oxytocin for induction. Worth knowing when documenting hyperstimulation and titrating oxytocin.

items.title: Reduced fetal movements: second edition of green-top guideline 57 published
items.why: The first full rewrite since 2011 (Whitworth et al, BJOG 2026): no formal kick counting, handheld Doppler first to exclude fetal death, computerised CTG from 26+0 weeks once viability is confirmed, and recurrent RFM flagged as higher risk for stillbirth, growth restriction and preterm birth. Check the full guideline against the Pocket O&G RFM pathway before relying on either.

items.title: Inhaled nitrous oxide reduces pain in outpatient operative hysteroscopy
items.why: A double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of 214 women (Razdolsky et al, Obstet Gynecol 2026) found self-administered nitrous oxide roughly halved intraprocedural pain, raised completion rates (94% vs 84%) and markedly improved satisfaction, with the largest effect in postmenopausal women. A cheap, familiar option if your outpatient hysteroscopy service struggles with pain-related abandonment.

items.title: Eclampsia across seven countries: 42% had no pre-eclampsia diagnosis before the first seizure
items.why: An individual participant data meta-analysis of 615 cases (Salvi et al, BJOG 2026) found a pooled incidence of 2.2 per 10,000 births in high-income countries, with only 42% of women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia before seizure onset and a third fitting for the first time postpartum. A reminder that eclampsia often arrives unheralded and that postnatal vigilance matters as much as antenatal surveillance.

items.title: Levemir (insulin detemir) to be discontinued: NICE flags it in diabetes in pregnancy guidance
items.why: NICE added a note to the diabetes in pregnancy guideline (NG3) in February 2026 highlighting that Levemir, a long-acting insulin commonly continued or started in pregnancy, is being discontinued. Women using it will need a planned switch, so check your local diabetes-in-pregnancy pathway for the preferred alternative.

items.title: No link between paracetamol in pregnancy and autism or ADHD, major meta-analysis finds
items.why: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 43 studies (Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women's Health 2026) found no association between prenatal paracetamol exposure and autism, ADHD or intellectual disability in the low-bias and sibling-controlled studies, concluding earlier signals were confounding. Useful when counselling women worried by claims from the US: paracetamol used as directed remains the first-line analgesic in pregnancy.

items.title: Cervical length still predicts preterm birth after 24 weeks, with a 25.5 mm cutoff
items.why: A meta-analysis of 16 studies and 26,776 pregnancies (Cheung et al, AJOG 2026) found transvaginal cervical length between 24 and 32 weeks remains discriminative in asymptomatic women, with a 25.5 to 26 mm cutoff giving a positive likelihood ratio of 7.75 for spontaneous preterm birth; the association disappears after about 31 weeks. Relevant to preterm surveillance clinics extending measurement beyond the classic mid-trimester window.
